messages.author: a08a2def4527ebe2
messages.subject: Max Depth in Shinystan
parts:
Hi!

I'm estimating many Stan-models using cmdstan, and then collecting results in R with Rstan. I set max treedepth to 100 (excessive, yes...). Attached is an example of output csv-file from cmdstan. 

I read the file in using  
post<- read_stan_csv("test.csv")

However, when I do 
ss <- as.shinystan(post)
retrieve(ss, "max_depth")

it gives "11". Shouldn't this be 100?!

I'm using shinystan 2.3.0 and Rstan 2.14.1

Thank you,
Ole-Petter

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Max Depth in Shinystan
parts:
On Wednesday, February 8, 2017 at 1:33:28 PM UTC-5, Ole Petter Hansen wrote:
However, when I do 
ss <- as.shinystan(post)
retrieve(ss, "max_depth")

it gives "11". Shouldn't this be 100?!
I think it is telling you that the largest treedepth__ among the post-warmup iterations was 11 rather than what max_treedepth was set to.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Max Depth in Shinystan
parts: In other words, what you're seeing is what actually happened.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Max Depth in Shinystan
parts:
It's a binary tree, so depth 100 is 2^100 nodes, where
each node requires a density and gradient calculation.

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Max Depth in Shinystan
parts:
Yup, what Bob says is true. Although the reason you are seeing shinystan report 11 instead of 100 is because when you actually ran the model it never reached the max depth of 100 you set. shinystan is reporting the max depth that was hit, not the max allowed depth. 

Jonah
